messages.content: You look at one picture with no other context and describe exactly what is drawn, like a careful field naturalist. Do not guess what was intended; describe only what is visible. description: a free paragraph describing the whole creature first. parts: every body part you see, one entry each (head, horns, ears, mane, legs, feet, tail, wings, gills, tentacles, shell, plates, scales, feathers, markings), with what it looks like and where it is. attached_objects: anything that looks attached to or sitting on the body rather than part of it, such as an object, an armor piece or a whole small animal; empty if none. animals: every real animal whose features you can see, as everyday English common names, at most four; include any animal that only one part resembles. Then count, looking carefully: separate_bodies: separate animal bodies or body-shaped objects in the picture, including any whole animal or animal-shaped object attached to or sitting on the main creature. heads: heads of any kind. walking_legs: legs the creature stands or walks on, including hidden ones you can infer. wings: wings of any kind. extra_limb_pieces: jointed leg-like, claw-like or tentacle-like pieces other than the walking legs and the tail. tails: tails of any kind (0 if none).

"description": "The creature is shown in right-facing profile standing on a small patch of dirt and sparse grass. It has the overall build of a large felid with a long torso, four sturdy legs, and a blunt muzzle, covered in short tan to light brown fur with faint darker spotting. Its head, chest, belly, legs and long furry tail are mammalian and cat-like, while its entire dorsal surface from the back of the neck to the base of the rump is covered by a contrasting mantle of dense, overlapping dark gray to black feathers with a bright yellow-orange patch on the side of the neck and a thin white border, giving the appearance of a penguin's body draped over the back. The feathered mantle ends in a small pointed dark tail just above the mammal's own tan tail. No wings, horns, or other appendages are visible beyond the four legs and the two tails.",
